06767F20-DACF-49AA-BABB-A11EBBE9A77D.name: Bruce Fordyce
06767F20-DACF-49AA-BABB-A11EBBE9A77D.bio: The greatest Comrades runner of all time. Fordyce won a record 9 times — 8 consecutive from 1981 to 1988, plus 1990 — and held the down-run record (5:24:07) for 21 years. He also held world records at 50 miles and 100km, and won the London to Brighton ultra three times. An outspoken anti-apartheid activist, he famously wore a black armband during his 1981 victory in protest. He later introduced parkrun to South Africa. His 30 Comrades finishes span from 1977 to 2014.

029A4E77-6078-4471-A460-EF6327651101.name: Alberto Salazar
029A4E77-6078-4471-A460-EF6327651101.bio: One of the greatest marathon runners in history. Salazar won three consecutive New York City Marathons (1980–82) and the 1982 Boston Marathon, setting an American record of 2:08:52. After retiring from road racing, he came out of retirement to attempt the Comrades — having never raced beyond marathon distance and doing all his long training runs on a treadmill. He won the 1994 Comrades in 5:38:39, later saying it was "more satisfying than anything I've done." He competed at the 1984 Olympics and later coached the Nike Oregon Project.

10B7ACE1-D68C-4577-A600-4138DC6ADA58.name: Yiannis Kouros
10B7ACE1-D68C-4577-A600-4138DC6ADA58.bio: Widely considered the greatest ultrarunner of all time. The Greek-Australian holds virtually every ultra world record from 100 miles to 1,000 miles, including the iconic 24-hour record of 303.5 km (188 miles) that stood for decades. He ran the Comrades just once, in 1998, finishing in 6:10:35 for a Silver medal — a remarkable result given his specialty in flat, multi-day events rather than the hilly Comrades course.

E1BC62E1-2191-4698-9256-CDC2AD1190B6.name: Camille Herron
E1BC62E1-2191-4698-9256-CDC2AD1190B6.bio: American ultrarunning star who holds multiple world records at 100 miles, 12 hours, and 24 hours. Won the Comrades women's race twice — in 2017 and 2022 — becoming the first American woman to win since Ann Trason 20 years earlier. In 2017, she arrived at Comrades with just eight weeks of training after a knee injury, yet still won. She also won Western States 100 in 2017, becoming the first woman since Trason to win both races in the same year.

5B73167C-8171-4DCF-B800-5AE76A5E5EDB.name: Ann Trason
5B73167C-8171-4DCF-B800-5AE76A5E5EDB.bio: Widely regarded as the greatest female ultrarunner in history. Trason won the Western States 100 a record 14 times and held world records at 50 miles, 100km, and 100 miles. She won the Comrades women's race in 1996 and 1997, the first American woman to do so. Sports Illustrated ranked her the 65th greatest female athlete of the 20th century. Her 1997 winning time of 5:58:25 remains one of the fastest women's Comrades times ever recorded.

724BF7D1-29E6-4B10-9BA1-ADCB726D654E.name: Wally Hayward
724BF7D1-29E6-4B10-9BA1-ADCB726D654E.bio: A Comrades legend whose career spanned 59 years. Hayward first won the race in 1930, then disappeared for 20 years — through the Great Depression, World War II, and the dawn of the apartheid era. When he returned in 1950, he didn't just finish — he won again, and went on to win three more times, setting a course record of 5:52:30 in 1953 at age 44. He competed at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics (marathon, finishing 10th) and earned a British Empire Medal for bravery during WW2. Most remarkably, he returned to race Comrades at age 79 in 1988 and 80 in 1989, earning Bronze medals both times.

816C5657-147E-4D33-8B6F-ED0EBDE4E35F.name: Jackie Mekler
816C5657-147E-4D33-8B6F-ED0EBDE4E35F.bio: Five-time Comrades winner (1958, 1960, 1963, 1964, 1968) and the first runner to break the 6-hour barrier on the up run, clocking 5:56:32 in 1960. Mekler accumulated 10 Gold medals across his Comrades career and also represented South Africa as an Olympic marathon runner. Raised in an orphanage, he took up running as a teenager and went on to become one of the defining figures of Comrades' golden era. His autobiography "Running Alone" was published shortly before his death in 2019 at age 87.

0D844D5E-725C-4AF3-92B4-DE7EAB18139D.name: Leonid Shvetsov
0D844D5E-725C-4AF3-92B4-DE7EAB18139D.bio: Russian two-time Comrades winner and two-time Olympian. Shvetsov competed in the Olympic marathon at both the 1996 Atlanta and 2004 Athens Games, with a marathon PB of 2:09:16. At Comrades, he broke Bruce Fordyce's 21-year-old down-run record with 5:20:49 in 2007, then set the up-run record of 5:24:49 in 2008 — a record that still stands. His twin victories were part of Russia's remarkable 2006–2008 dominance of the race.

9A265EF1-7118-4F4E-8C78-C8392FFB8ED2.name: Zola Budd Pieterse
9A265EF1-7118-4F4E-8C78-C8392FFB8ED2.bio: South African-born runner famous for the dramatic collision with Mary Decker at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics 3000m final, one of the most iconic moments in Olympic history. A barefoot running phenomenon, she held the 5000m world record and competed at two Olympics (1984 for Great Britain, 1992 for South Africa). She took on the Comrades decades later, earning a Gold medal in 2014 by finishing 7th woman in 6:55:55 — an achievement she called one of her career highlights. She ran alongside Bruce Fordyce at his 30th Comrades in 2012.

3A01F893-E6A1-4612-B394-D9AED26F986C.name: Elena Nurgalieva
3A01F893-E6A1-4612-B394-D9AED26F986C.bio: Russian twin who holds the record for the most women's Comrades victories — 8 in total — and earned 13 consecutive Gold medals from 2003 to 2015. Together with her identical twin sister Olesya (2 wins), the Nurgalieva sisters won 10 Comrades titles between them and anchored Russia's extraordinary 11-year women's winning streak (2003–2013). They also led Russia to 8 women's podium sweeps during that era, the only country other than South Africa to achieve the feat.

7C020BD7-1410-4A2D-BE80-A907F7A797EE.name: Olesya Nurgalieva
7C020BD7-1410-4A2D-BE80-A907F7A797EE.bio: Russian ultrarunner who won the women's Comrades twice (2007, 2009). Identical twin sister of Elena Nurgalieva (8× winner), together they won 10 Comrades between them. The Nurgalieva twins are the most dominant sibling duo in Comrades history, anchoring Russia's 11-year winning streak in the women's race (2003-2013).

D5BA88E7-513F-4AA4-A10B-1819D3E0F5AB.name: Sam Tshabalala
D5BA88E7-513F-4AA4-A10B-1819D3E0F5AB.bio: A railway worker from Mpumalanga who became a national hero when he won the 1989 Comrades in 5:35:51, becoming the first Black winner of the race — a deeply symbolic moment during apartheid. His victory was watched by millions on television and became a watershed moment in South African sport, demonstrating that talent transcends racial barriers. He went on to complete 13 Comrades before his death in 2022 at age 65.

AA44A8AA-1248-4228-8439-77B6FAF6BEBE.name: Frith van der Merwe
AA44A8AA-1248-4228-8439-77B6FAF6BEBE.bio: Three-time Comrades women's winner (1988, 1989, 1991) who became the first woman to break the 6-hour barrier, running 5:54:43 on the down run in 1989. That record stood for an extraordinary 34 years until Gerda Steyn broke it in 2023. She is considered one of the greatest female ultrarunners South Africa has produced.

ADC35239-1375-40A3-9E6C-32A8C536E32E.name: Gerda Steyn
ADC35239-1375-40A3-9E6C-32A8C536E32E.bio: The dominant force in modern women's Comrades, Steyn holds both the women's up-run record (5:49:46, 2024) and down-run record (5:44:54, 2023), breaking Frith van der Merwe's 34-year-old down-run record. She was the first woman to run sub-6 hours on the up run. With 4 victories (2019, 2023, 2024, 2025) and counting, she is also the South African women's marathon record holder (2:24:03).

34459797-8B4D-4D1B-BD21-3AB7131C4293.name: Bongmusa Mthembu
34459797-8B4D-4D1B-BD21-3AB7131C4293.bio: Three-time Comrades winner (2014, 2017, 2018) from rural KwaZulu-Natal, where he worked as a bricklayer before becoming a professional runner. Mthembu has earned 11 Gold medals — tied with Bruce Fordyce for the most by a male runner — and holds the South African 100km record. His story of rising from manual labour to ultrarunning stardom is one of the great Comrades narratives.

085FCC36-DBCD-4330-B1D0-42CDA43F3169.name: Tete Dijana
085FCC36-DBCD-4330-B1D0-42CDA43F3169.bio: Holds the fastest Comrades Marathon time ever recorded — 5:13:58, set on the 2023 down run. A three-time winner (2022, 2023, 2025), Dijana has established himself as the fastest man in Comrades history, with his 2023 time setting a standard that may stand for years to come.

A895E657-8A92-443E-AC0F-201EB57A8395.name: Frances Hayward
A895E657-8A92-443E-AC0F-201EB57A8395.bio: The first woman to complete the Comrades Marathon, finishing in 11:35:00 in 1923 — only the third running of the race. She finished 28th overall in a field of 30 runners who started. Her pioneering run came decades before women's participation became officially recognised.

2C8F70E5-2883-4DDF-932B-E50E3F638EBF.name: Gordon Ramsay
2C8F70E5-2883-4DDF-932B-E50E3F638EBF.bio: The world-renowned celebrity chef and TV personality ran 5 Comrades Marathons between 2000 and 2004, finishing 3 of them with Bronze medals. Bruce Fordyce wrote about meeting Ramsay at the 2000 Comrades expo, and Ramsay later said Comrades was "my favourite race and the toughest I have ever run." He is also an Ironman triathlon finisher.

DA52CF3E-CF7F-4438-8BC5-E5B63E9F4E96.name: Tim Noakes
DA52CF3E-CF7F-4438-8BC5-E5B63E9F4E96.bio: Globally renowned sports scientist and author of 'The Lore of Running', the definitive textbook on running science. Professor Noakes ran 7 Comrades Marathons, earning a best of Silver (6:49:00 in 1973). His experiences racing and studying the Comrades partly inspired his groundbreaking Central Governor Theory of exercise physiology. He described the Comrades as "the Super Bowl of South African sports."

AEBC0F33-8804-40A4-9237-9358C61C9FD0.name: Kabelo Mabalane
AEBC0F33-8804-40A4-9237-9358C61C9FD0.bio: South African kwaito music star (TKZee), TV personality, and pastor who has completed 13 Comrades Marathons. Mabalane has spoken publicly about how running saved him from substance abuse, a story he told in his book 'I Ran For My Life'. His best time of 7:54:57 (2019) earned him a Bill Rowan medal, and his progression from a 10:51 Bronze to sub-8 hours shows remarkable dedication.

D9621A8A-03B5-41B2-9669-3B1456811CA8.name: Charly Doll
D9621A8A-03B5-41B2-9669-3B1456811CA8.bio: German ultrarunner who made history as the first non-South African men's winner in 72 years when he won the 1993 Comrades in 5:39:41. His victory broke South Africa's monopoly on the men's title that had lasted since the race's inception in 1921. He returned to defend his title in 1994 but was defeated by Alberto Salazar.
tags: First Non-SA Men's Winner in 72 Years

D8BACC72-EFA3-4223-960A-175AFDB8CE93.name: Jaroslaw Janicki
D8BACC72-EFA3-4223-960A-175AFDB8CE93.bio: Polish ultra marathon legend who won the 1999 Comrades and remained a remarkably consistent top finisher over 12+ years. His 16 Comrades entries from 1996 to 2012 included multiple Gold medals and top-10 finishes, making him one of the most successful European runners in the race's history.

CCA19011-A181-4079-B8D5-88B63DABE02C.name: David Gatebe
CCA19011-A181-4079-B8D5-88B63DABE02C.bio: South African ultrarunner who holds the men's down-run course record of 5:18:19, set in 2016 — the second-fastest Comrades time ever at the time. His explosive win established him as one of the most talented runners in the race's modern era.

D5B1F1FB-04DE-40E4-9522-A3110550F5A0.name: Piet Wiersma
D5B1F1FB-04DE-40E4-9522-A3110550F5A0.bio: Dutch ultrarunner who became only the second European men's winner in 30 years when he won the 2024 Comrades. He was also runner-up in both 2023 (with a blistering 5:14:01, just seconds behind Tete Dijana's all-time record) and 2025, demonstrating remarkable consistency at the highest level.

645F182A-87F4-40C4-807D-01AC86178CFE.name: Wynand Claassen
645F182A-87F4-40C4-807D-01AC86178CFE.bio: Captained the South African Springbok rugby team from 1981 to 1983, then turned his endurance to ultrarunning, completing 11 Comrades Marathons between 1985 and 2000. His father George Claassen won the Comrades in 1961, making them one of the few father-son Comrades champions in the race's history.

10AD14FB-466F-4C51-BA08-0F28198C864B.name: Ellie Greenwood
10AD14FB-466F-4C51-BA08-0F28198C864B.bio: Canadian-British ultrarunner who won the women's Comrades in 2014 (6:18:15) and finished 2nd in 2012 (6:08:24). A dominant force in trail ultrarunning, Greenwood won the Western States 100 in 2012 (setting a new course record of 16:47:19) and 2014. She also won the IAU 100km World Championship in 2012. Known as one of the most versatile ultrarunners of her generation, excelling on both road and trail.

45792395-ADFE-434A-B2A6-3A96C0D3B68D.name: Caroline Wöstmann
45792395-ADFE-434A-B2A6-3A96C0D3B68D.bio: South African runner who won the women's Comrades in 2015 (6:12:22) and earned multiple Gold medals racing under her maiden name Caroline Cherry. Born in Germany, she became a South African citizen and one of the country's top female ultrarunners. She also won the 2015 Two Oceans Marathon, completing the rare Comrades-Two Oceans double in the same year. Her 2016 Comrades (2nd place, 6:30:44) confirmed her as one of the top women of her era.

27239E7D-E271-406B-AAA7-C5F7D614FA3C.name: Arthur Newton
27239E7D-E271-406B-AAA7-C5F7D614FA3C.bio: English-born pioneer who dominated the early Comrades, winning 5 times (1922-27). He only took up running at age 38 as a protest — running from his farm to Pietermaritzburg to draw attention to a land compensation dispute. Newton revolutionised distance running with high-mileage training and set world records at 50 miles, 100 miles, and 24 hours. He had to cut back on his 20-year smoking habit to train. He later moved to England where he mentored a generation of ultrarunners.

92BAFEC0-B382-4126-B9C0-C34B898DC02D.name: Hardy Ballington
92BAFEC0-B382-4126-B9C0-C34B898DC02D.bio: Five-time Comrades winner (1933, 1934, 1936, 1938, 1947), spanning both sides of World War II. Ballington was one of the great pre-war runners who returned after the 6-year wartime hiatus to win again in 1947. His rivalry with Wally Hayward defined the mid-century era of the race.

324F44D4-37FC-439D-9209-4E4846F87466.name: Bill Rowan
324F44D4-37FC-439D-9209-4E4846F87466.bio: Winner of the inaugural Comrades Marathon in 1921, completing the first-ever race in 8:59:00. A World War I veteran, Rowan responded to Vic Clapham's call for an endurance event to honour fallen comrades. The Bill Rowan medal (sub-9 hours on the up run, sub-7:30 on the down) is named in his honour — one of the most coveted achievements in the race.

32909030-373B-4ABA-8202-8B4F00630014.name: Dave Bagshaw
32909030-373B-4ABA-8202-8B4F00630014.bio: Three-time consecutive Comrades winner (1969-1971) who set the course record with 5:45:35 in 1969. Bagshaw was the dominant force of the late 1960s and early 1970s, winning in an era when the race was growing rapidly in popularity.

E4340967-B3CE-4DF7-934E-147537656DC2.name: Alan Robb
E4340967-B3CE-4DF7-934E-147537656DC2.bio: Four-time Comrades winner (1976-78, 1980) who set the then-course record of 5:29:14 in 1978. Robb dominated the late 1970s before Bruce Fordyce's era began. A smooth, efficient runner known for his tactical racing style.

53498112-A120-4DE3-AF90-7F37067A10EC.name: Vladimir Kotov
53498112-A120-4DE3-AF90-7F37067A10EC.bio: Russian runner who won the Comrades three times (2000, 2002, 2004), part of the remarkable Russian dominance of the early 2000s. His 2000 winning time of 5:25:33 was the fastest in a decade. Along with Shvetsov, Grishin, and Kharitonov, Kotov was part of a Russian golden era that saw their runners win 7 of 9 men's races from 1996 to 2008.

7353CD81-E5E3-4BF3-BD4F-575E0F8C8235.name: Stephen Muzhingi
7353CD81-E5E3-4BF3-BD4F-575E0F8C8235.bio: Zimbabwean runner who won three consecutive Comrades (2009-2011), the first to achieve this since Fordyce. A former barber from Harare, Muzhingi's rise from humble beginnings to Comrades champion captured imaginations. He was the first non-South African winner since Janicki (1999) and only the second foreign runner to win three times.

CBB2B390-7EDE-4039-B8F4-BD689D4713FC.name: Bob de la Motte
CBB2B390-7EDE-4039-B8F4-BD689D4713FC.bio: Five-time Comrades medallist (including 3 golds) who had epic duels with Bruce Fordyce in the 1980s. De la Motte finished 2nd to Fordyce in both 1984 (5:30:59) and 1986 (5:26:12), with his 1986 time just 2 minutes behind Fordyce's course record. He emigrated to Australia and wrote 'Runaway Comrade,' a memoir covering his career, allegations, and apartheid-era sport. Proceeds from the book benefit black ultra-marathon runners from the 1974-90 era.

FBEEA608-B6B8-4F59-8AAE-CDE3BBC37579.name: Charl Mattheus
FBEEA608-B6B8-4F59-8AAE-CDE3BBC37579.bio: A phenomenal South African runner who crossed the line first in the 1992 Comrades but was disqualified after testing positive for a banned stimulant — a substance that was later removed from the prohibited list, making the disqualification a controversial technicality. He proved his class beyond any doubt by finishing 2nd in 1995 (5:35:01), winning outright in 1997 (5:28:37), and finishing 2nd again in 1998. One of the finest runners of his generation, Mattheus competed in an era of intense international competition.

CC583A79-A72B-4EE2-AF84-DCB6050F990F.name: Dmitri Grishin
CC583A79-A72B-4EE2-AF84-DCB6050F990F.bio: Russian runner who won the Comrades twice (1996, 1998). Grishin was part of the wave of talented Russian ultrarunners who dominated the race in the late 1990s and 2000s. His 1998 winning time of 5:26:25 was one of the fastest of the decade.

1DC5EBC9-1240-4930-B506-5F8EF5AF6FA9.name: Nick Bester
1DC5EBC9-1240-4930-B506-5F8EF5AF6FA9.bio: Won the 1991 Comrades down run in 5:40:53 and earned 9 Gold medals across a 16-year career. Nicknamed 'The Iron Man,' Bester started running at 24 to get fit for rugby. After retiring from competitive racing, he became manager of Nedbank Running Club, where he identifies development athletes from age 15 — saying it takes 'at least ten years of continuous development' to reach peak performance. He was runner-up three times (1994, 1996, 1997) and placed in the top 10 for over a decade.

83A21C2A-355F-4FDD-8730-384BD1FA8C3E.name: Ludwick Mamabolo
83A21C2A-355F-4FDD-8730-384BD1FA8C3E.bio: South African runner who won the 2012 Comrades in 5:31:03. Mamabolo was a consistent top-5 finisher, placing 2nd three times (2010, 2014, 2016). His 2016 second-place time of 5:24:05 was faster than many winning times, but he was beaten by David Gatebe's extraordinary 5:18:19 course record.

F2B10C6A-00C0-49A5-97B9-8141D56376CC.name: Claude Moshiywa
F2B10C6A-00C0-49A5-97B9-8141D56376CC.bio: South African runner who won the 2013 Comrades in 5:32:09. Known for his aggressive early pace and gutsy racing style. Moshiywa accumulated 18 finishes across a career spanning 2000-2025, consistently competing at the highest level for over two decades.

E210AA4E-9D86-4ED0-A0A3-DD168BE7C412.name: Edward Mothibi
E210AA4E-9D86-4ED0-A0A3-DD168BE7C412.bio: South African runner who won the 2019 Comrades in 5:31:33 and has been a consistent top finisher throughout the 2020s. Mothibi placed 2nd in 2022, 3rd in 2023, and 4th in 2025, demonstrating remarkable longevity at the elite level. His 2023 time of 5:17:34 (3rd place) was one of the fastest ever recorded.

DB8D23E8-89B4-41E3-9085-280CA2EF9A67.name: Shaun Meiklejohn
DB8D23E8-89B4-41E3-9085-280CA2EF9A67.bio: Won the 1995 Comrades in 5:34:02 and holds one of the most remarkable longevity records in the race. Meiklejohn has accumulated 33 finishes spanning from 1982 to 2025 — over four decades of Comrades running. His consistency and dedication epitomise the spirit of the race.

DEEFF9E1-0805-4AAC-A462-9A64B016CB0E.name: Andrew Kelehe
DEEFF9E1-0805-4AAC-A462-9A64B016CB0E.bio: South African runner who won the 2001 Comrades in 5:25:52. Brother of Gift Kelehe (2015 winner), the Kelehe brothers are one of the few sibling pairs to both win the Comrades.

A416BCC7-C113-4034-97EC-167696879EB4.name: Gift Kelehe
A416BCC7-C113-4034-97EC-167696879EB4.bio: South African runner who won the 2015 Comrades in 5:38:36. Brother of Andrew Kelehe (2001 winner), making them one of the few sibling pairs to both win the race.

25357FAE-D998-4082-991E-C15CACE6F250.name: Fusi Nhlapo
25357FAE-D998-4082-991E-C15CACE6F250.bio: South African runner who won the 2003 Comrades in 5:28:53. Nhlapo was a consistent top-10 finisher for a decade, with 9 gold medals between 2000 and 2010. He finished in the top 6 for six consecutive years, an extraordinary run of consistency at the highest level.

7D0C79D3-8764-47B1-BC25-C0160B3C11DF.name: Bart Yasso
7D0C79D3-8764-47B1-BC25-C0160B3C11DF.bio: Known as the 'Mayor of Running,' Yasso is Runner's World magazine's legendary Chief Running Officer. Famous for inventing the 'Yasso 800s' marathon predictor workout, he has completed races on all seven continents. He ran the 2010 Comrades in 11:33:38 (Vic Clapham medal), calling it the most profound race of his life.

FEE5F3C4-B67D-4185-ADED-A1BE094B43C3.name: Oleg Kharitonov
FEE5F3C4-B67D-4185-ADED-A1BE094B43C3.bio: Russian runner who won the 2006 Comrades in 5:35:19, continuing Russia's dominance of the men's race. Kharitonov was one of several elite Russian ultrarunners who targeted the Comrades during the early 2000s.

5CBB8BB3-769C-455D-A00F-812192E32E41.name: Sipho Ngomane
5CBB8BB3-769C-455D-A00F-812192E32E41.bio: South African runner who won the 2005 Comrades in 5:27:11. Ngomane's career was marked by dramatic highs and lows — after his victory he suffered numerous DNFs in subsequent years but kept returning, embodying the Comrades never-give-up spirit.

FC101EEC-B352-4778-9BDA-F1A033290337.name: George Claassen
FC101EEC-B352-4778-9BDA-F1A033290337.bio: Won the 1961 Comrades in 6:07:07. Father of Wynand Claassen (Springbok rugby captain), making them a unique father-son Comrades dynasty — George as winner, Wynand as an 11-time finisher. The Claassen family story spans two generations of South African sporting achievement.

126C8C8A-D0F2-4766-AE12-4302D7B831FE.name: Mavis Hutchison
126C8C8A-D0F2-4766-AE12-4302D7B831FE.bio: Pioneer of women's ultra-distance running, nicknamed 'The Galloping Granny.' Won the women's Comrades in 1965 and 1966, decades before women were fully accepted in the race. In 1978, at age 53, she became the first woman to run across America coast to coast. She was initially denied official entry and had to fight for women's inclusion.
tags: First Woman to Run Across America

3D70896F-A8FB-4099-9505-1B44355FFAF1.name: Betty Cavanagh
3D70896F-A8FB-4099-9505-1B44355FFAF1.bio: Four-time women's Comrades winner (1970-72, 1975) who dominated the early era of women's participation. Cavanagh helped establish women as legitimate competitors in the race during a time when female ultrarunners were still a rarity worldwide.

5A22BAE8-7DA5-42C4-B8FD-8B4B79AAF419.name: Isavel Roche-Kelly
5A22BAE8-7DA5-42C4-B8FD-8B4B79AAF419.bio: Irish-born runner who won the women's Comrades twice (1980-81). Her 1981 winning time of 6:44:35 was a huge leap forward for women's performances at the race. Roche-Kelly was the first international woman to win the Comrades.

75307334-E727-486A-BE3E-C0A2B19CEE4C.name: Helen Lucre
75307334-E727-486A-BE3E-C0A2B19CEE4C.bio: Three-time consecutive women's Comrades winner (1985-87). Lucre dominated the mid-1980s women's race during a transitional period between the pioneer era and the modern professional era that began with Frith van der Merwe.

BAB35012-BC3D-4DD9-AB6E-8907CBC40AE1.name: Maria Bak
BAB35012-BC3D-4DD9-AB6E-8907CBC40AE1.bio: Russian runner who won the women's Comrades three times (1995, 2000, 2002). Bak was part of the Russian dominance of the race, winning across an impressive 7-year span. Her 2000 winning time of 6:15:35 was one of the era's fastest.

F8B34ECE-E448-445B-BC77-8F9014834DF9.name: Charne Bosman
F8B34ECE-E448-445B-BC77-8F9014834DF9.bio: South African runner who won the 2016 women's Comrades in 6:25:55. Bosman competed alongside Gerda Steyn and Caroline Wöstmann in one of the strongest eras of South African women's ultrarunning.

322BC87A-E5D3-4626-9E72-B0F073DBD4F9.name: Ann Ashworth
322BC87A-E5D3-4626-9E72-B0F073DBD4F9.bio: South African runner who won the 2018 women's Comrades in 6:10:04. Ashworth's win was a popular result among the Comrades community after years of consistent high-level performances.

C9B6438B-AFCA-4CB9-93E0-841EA2BD7A0C.name: Birgit Lennartz
C9B6438B-AFCA-4CB9-93E0-841EA2BD7A0C.bio: German ultrarunner who won the 1999 women's Comrades in 6:31:03. Lennartz was a multiple IAU World Championship competitor and one of Europe's top female ultrarunners in the 1990s.

4C0A7938-EB0F-4852-918E-7C0A36705618.name: Hoseah Tjale
4C0A7938-EB0F-4852-918E-7C0A36705618.bio: Pioneering Black ultrarunner who placed 2nd twice (1985, 1990), 3rd twice (1986, 1987), and earned 9 Gold medals across 13 Comrades finishes. He won the Two Oceans Marathon (1980) and London to Brighton ultra (1985). Bruce Fordyce called him one of the greatest runners never to win the Comrades. As an amateur during the apartheid era, he never received prize money.

16D7BB73-B435-4FA3-93D4-2FCAD156F81E.name: Willie Mtolo
16D7BB73-B435-4FA3-93D4-2FCAD156F81E.bio: Won the 1992 New York City Marathon (2:09:29), the first South African to win NYC, and was named SA Sportsman of the Year. He finished 2nd at the 1989 Comrades behind Sam Tshabalala in 5:39:00. Marathon PB of 2:08:15. Banned from international competition until 1992 due to the apartheid sports boycott. He now runs a charitable athletic academy in KwaZulu-Natal townships.

41210171-3F87-4230-B039-51D4735CEED3.name: Tilda Tearle
41210171-3F87-4230-B039-51D4735CEED3.bio: Won the 1993 women's Comrades and completed 30 finishes (Triple Green Number holder). An iconic figure known for her blonde pigtails and ever-present smile, Tearle progressed from 4th to 3rd to 2nd to 1st over four consecutive years before her victory. With 10 top-10 finishes, she epitomises the dedication and spirit of the Comrades community.

90672B12-BD32-46F2-9C56-3B566AA05736.name: Alexandra Morozova
90672B12-BD32-46F2-9C56-3B566AA05736.bio: Russian runner who won the 2022 women's Comrades in 6:17:48 after going to court for the right to race (initially barred because of Russia's invasion of Ukraine). She has earned 5 Gold medals from 5 starts, with runner-up finishes in 2017 and 2019. Coached by former winner Oleg Kharitonov.

185CEF6E-BE46-4867-84B3-EF9F1C6A9330.name: Jetman Msuthu
185CEF6E-BE46-4867-84B3-EF9F1C6A9330.bio: Declared the winner of the 1992 Comrades Marathon after the original winner, Charl Mattheus, was disqualified for a doping violation — the only time in Comrades history that a victory has been revoked. Msuthu never carried the winner's baton and is believed to be the only champion who did not learn he had won on the day of the race itself. The second Black winner after Sam Tshabalala (1989), Msuthu completed 14 Comrades finishes and represented South Africa at the 100km World Championships, earning team gold. Born near Bizana in the Eastern Cape.

54FE2430-709B-4E32-82A7-2F9389F122C3.name: Louis Massyn
54FE2430-709B-4E32-82A7-2F9389F122C3.bio: Holds the record for the most Comrades finishes ever — 50 completions achieved in 2025 at age 74. He started in 1973 at age 22 with a personal best of 6:25 (1981). He only missed the COVID years (2020-21) and 2022 (knee injury) across his extraordinary 52-year career. He raises funds for children with special needs.

921188D3-7ED4-4A98-B3F8-4B255A622710.name: Johannes Mosehla
921188D3-7ED4-4A98-B3F8-4B255A622710.bio: The oldest person ever to finish the Comrades Marathon, completing the 2025 race at age 83 in 11:47:10. A bricklayer from Polokwane who started running in 1963, he couldn't enter the Comrades as a young man due to apartheid. He broke Wally Hayward's 34-year-old age record in 2023 at age 81. Won Limpopo Sport Star of the Year.

673EF5A9-5C8A-4027-B78F-79C431288957.name: Nao Kazami
673EF5A9-5C8A-4027-B78F-79C431288957.bio: Japanese ultrarunner who held the men's 100km world record (6:09:14, set 2018). He finished 3rd at the 2019 Comrades in 5:39:16, the best-ever finish by a Japanese (and Asian) athlete. Marathon PB of 2:13:13. Remarkably, he trains while working full-time at an auto parts company, starting his runs at 5am.

CE68BD37-F858-4576-9900-AE2C34FEF427.name: Lettie van Zyl
CE68BD37-F858-4576-9900-AE2C34FEF427.bio: Three consecutive women's Comrades winner (1976-78). First member of the women's Hat Trick Club. In 1975 she actually finished first but was stripped of the win for not meeting qualifying standards. Along with Betty Cavanagh and Mavis Hutchison, she was a genuine trailblazer for women in the race.

0C8FBA92-BD8F-4BF7-B96D-0EF517062A48.name: Lindsay Weight
0C8FBA92-BD8F-4BF7-B96D-0EF517062A48.bio: New Zealand-born runner who won the women's Comrades twice (1983-84). Part of the growing international field of women competitors in the early 1980s, Weight helped raise the standard of women's performances in the race.

16FB969F-C3C6-4E1F-B7C1-E1BDE28E7510.name: Colleen De Reuck
16FB969F-C3C6-4E1F-B7C1-E1BDE28E7510.bio: Four-time Olympian (1992, 1996, 2000 for South Africa; 2004 for USA) and holder of the South African women's marathon record (2:26:35). She won the US Olympic Marathon Trials at age 40 in 2004. De Reuck made her Comrades debut at age 52 in 2016, finishing 8th woman with a Gold medal (6:50:21), and returned in 2017 for another Gold. Also an Ironman World Championship age-group winner.

27787E42-1097-4C66-9E1A-1AFE061A89FB.name: Dominika Stelmach
27787E42-1097-4C66-9E1A-1AFE061A89FB.bio: Polish ultrarunner who has been a consistent top-5 women's finisher since 2019. Stelmach placed 2nd in the 2022 women's Comrades (6:25:09) and has earned 5 consecutive Gold medals. One of the strongest European women in the modern era of the race.

BF862196-7C98-4CD9-8406-04B810AB6D5E.name: Valentina Shatyayeva
BF862196-7C98-4CD9-8406-04B810AB6D5E.bio: Russian ultrarunner who earned 9 consecutive Gold medals (1994-2002), one of the most consistent women's performers in Comrades history. Part of the Russian wave that dominated the women's race from the mid-1990s through the 2000s, she was a perennial podium threat alongside Maria Bak and Elvira Kolpakova.

83A4A9F8-A698-47A0-B7B4-4D235D74EB4F.name: Dave Levick
83A4A9F8-A698-47A0-B7B4-4D235D74EB4F.bio: Won the 1973 Comrades, making him the only Jewish winner in the race's history. His victory is chronicled in a Tablet Magazine feature exploring how the Comrades became a vehicle for Jewish immigrant integration into South African society.

5D585131-B601-47EB-8059-AE79EABA02C2.name: Amby Burfoot
5D585131-B601-47EB-8059-AE79EABA02C2.bio: Won the 1968 Boston Marathon and went on to become Editor-in-Chief of Runner's World magazine, where he championed the Comrades Marathon to international audiences. His 2015 Runner's World article remains one of the most widely-read English-language pieces about the race. He ran the Comrades twice — in 1993 (Bronze, 9:50:49) and 2006 (Vic Clapham, 11:05:03) — and has called it one of the most meaningful races of his life.

88EC664D-1A89-4EFF-A65B-A96982B16D69.name: Lindsey Parry
88EC664D-1A89-4EFF-A65B-A96982B16D69.bio: The official Comrades Marathon coach and founder of the Coach Parry online coaching platform (coachparry.com), which has guided thousands of runners to their Comrades finish. Together with Brad Nadauld, he runs a coaching business that has become the go-to resource for Comrades preparation. A dedicated runner himself with multiple finishes including Silver medals.

02FE5F11-9157-44F6-8DB7-E96D5301F4E0.name: Brad Nadauld
02FE5F11-9157-44F6-8DB7-E96D5301F4E0.bio: Co-founder and key figure in the Coach Parry coaching business alongside Lindsey Parry, the official Comrades Marathon coach. The Coach Parry platform has become one of the most trusted resources for Comrades Marathon training and preparation.

A36C0645-B7D1-40A7-BC97-6DB26DE23C2A.name: Stuart Mann
A36C0645-B7D1-40A7-BC97-6DB26DE23C2A.bio: South African data journalist and Comrades analyst known as 'The Running Mann.' His website runningmann.co.za has become the definitive source for Comrades Marathon statistical analysis, featuring innovative visualizations like the 'Christmas tree' medal clustering pattern and hurricane funnel attrition charts. A dedicated Comrades runner himself with 10 finishes and a Green Number spanning over two decades.

7104B74C-EDEF-4504-A029-134D8199D3A7.name: Dave Adams
7104B74C-EDEF-4504-A029-134D8199D3A7.bio: Self-taught running coach who has masterminded Nedbank Running Club's modern Comrades dynasty. Starting his coaching career while working at Impala Platinum mines, Adams has developed champions including Tete Dijana (down-run record holder), David Gatebe (2016 record 5:18:19), Edward Mothibi (2019 winner), and Gordon Lesetedi. In 2022, his athletes swept the men's podium 1-2-3. Described by his athletes as 'a mentor, friend, and father,' Adams is widely regarded as the most successful Comrades coach of the modern era.

E9E2EF22-FCBB-40D5-B71A-151D9BAB41D2.name: Derek Preiss
E9E2EF22-FCBB-40D5-B71A-151D9BAB41D2.bio: Won the 1974 and 1975 Comrades for Westville Athletic Club. Just 19 when he placed 6th at the SA Marathon Championships, Preiss was famously fuelled by a pre-race meal of chicken, milk tart, chocolate, fried eggs and toast before his 1974 victory (6:02:49). He vowed never to run again, then came back and won a second time in 5:53:50.

7BF70BC3-F1A5-4E93-9DCC-39E703D6E11D.name: Manie Kuhn
7BF70BC3-F1A5-4E93-9DCC-39E703D6E11D.bio: Won the 1967 Comrades in the closest finish in race history — beating Tommy Malone by a single second (5:54:10 to 5:54:11) after 90 kilometres of racing. Malone famously stumbled and fell inches from the finishing tape. A Savages AC legend, Kuhn completed 21 Comrades between 1960 and 1982.

B98455C1-2E12-4A25-AF02-C321ACCB492F.name: Mercer Davies
B98455C1-2E12-4A25-AF02-C321ACCB492F.bio: Won the 1957 Comrades for Germiston Callies Harriers, contributing to the club's dynasty of champions. Part of the golden era that saw Germiston Callies produce five different Comrades winners between 1930 and 1980.

8B050B84-371D-400C-ACB0-9E978BDF0995.name: Morris Alexander
8B050B84-371D-400C-ACB0-9E978BDF0995.bio: South African journalist and author of 'The Comrades Marathon Story,' one of the definitive histories of the race. His book chronicles the race from its founding in 1921 through the apartheid era, documenting the stories of pioneers, champions, and the social significance of the event. Alexander completed 7 Comrades between 1939 and 1952.

27A8966D-EAE6-41E0-84AF-B94251F79F40.name: John Cameron-Dow
27A8966D-EAE6-41E0-84AF-B94251F79F40.bio: Author of 'Comrades Marathon: The Ultimate Human Race,' a comprehensive history of the Comrades Marathon published in 2011. Cameron-Dow's book is widely regarded as the most complete modern history of the race, covering its century of existence with rich narrative and research. A dedicated Comrades runner himself, he completed 18 finishes between 1984 and 2005.

2F42DD88-8698-4B6A-BD99-CC2E379C18A2.name: Cherie Turner
2F42DD88-8698-4B6A-BD99-CC2E379C18A2.bio: Host of the 'Women's Running Stories' podcast, which features interviews with women runners sharing their experiences in ultramarathon running and the Comrades Marathon. A Comrades runner herself with two finishes, Turner brings a unique perspective as both a participant and storyteller, amplifying women's voices in the ultrarunning community.

31D6B838-C0CC-4EF0-91DE-A4695F7F6BBC.name: Don Oliver
31D6B838-C0CC-4EF0-91DE-A4695F7F6BBC.bio: Legendary Comrades coach and author of 'Make Sure of Your Comrades Medal,' the classic training guide that has helped thousands of novices achieve their Comrades dream. His philosophy of 'biteable bits and chewable chunks' — gradual progression — became the standard approach for first-time Comrades runners. Oliver earned 19 Comrades medals himself across 21 entries between 1978 and 1998, and guided countless runners to the finish line as a coach.
